title: Brainomix 360 Stroke AI supports immediate stroke identification at Royal Berkshire Hospital; 83-year-old transferred for thrombectomy within 25 minutes
summary: AI-supported scan identified Jean Hines's major stroke on arrival; transferred in 25 minutes for successful thrombectomy; good recovery.
account: Jean Hines, 83, collapsed at home and was taken to the Royal Berkshire Hospital, Reading, England, on a weekend in August (NHS England's December 2025 statement gives no year; 2025 is inferred). A scan carried out immediately on arrival, supported by the Brainomix AI imaging tool, identified a major stroke needing urgent specialist treatment. Within 25 minutes of reaching the emergency department she was on her way by ambulance to the John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford, where she had a successful mechanical thrombectomy; she describes a very good physical recovery with no serious disabilities. NHS England states the Brainomix 360 Stroke tool is used in over 70 hospitals and was associated with a 64-minute door-in-door-out reduction at primary stroke centers.
purpose: Brainomix 360 Stroke is built to analyze stroke imaging and support rapid treatment and transfer decisions, including selection for thrombectomy; this is its intended function.
taxonomy_note: Closest fit: the documented benefit is time saved in the transfer pathway. Protective response with prevention unproven because a major stroke was in progress and the AI-supported pathway had her on her way to the thrombectomy center within 25 minutes of arrival, but no source shows that the AI changed the outcome for this patient; the counterfactual rests only on the population-level 64-minute door-in-door-out association. the date observed uses the first day of August 2025; the release, published 2 December 2025, gives only 'a weekend in August' and no year, so 2025 is inferred.

ratings.reason: Rapid transfer enabled thrombectomy for a major stroke and she reports no serious disabilities; the AI's share of this outcome is the time saved, so -3 rather than -4.

NHS England reports a 25-minute door-in-door-out for this patient against a 64-minute average reduction at primary stroke centers and a doubling of thrombectomy rates (2.3% to 4.6%) at participating sites.

ai_role.statement: The AI-supported scan read identified the major stroke immediately on arrival, enabling a 25-minute door-in-door-out; the treatment itself (thrombectomy) was delivered by the Oxford team. The stroke would very likely have been diagnosed without AI, so the AI's contribution is the speed of decision and transfer, supported at population level by the Lancet Digital Health study (which has Brainomix co-authors alongside NHS lead authors).

evidence.quote: Stroke AI imaging software was associated with increased endovascular thrombectomy rates across the English NHS.

produced_by: AI stroke imaging with results available to the admitting team immediately after the scan
A regional transfer pathway from primary stroke center to a thrombectomy center
must_hold: Rapid ambulance transfer and an available thrombectomy team
Clinicians act on the AI-supported read without waiting for a separate specialist report

echoes.setting: 107 NHS hospitals in England, 452,952 stroke patients 2019-2023: thrombectomy rates doubled (2.3% to 4.6%) at AI evaluation sites (population-level)
